name: hidden_hanging_body_is_visible
why: ENTRY Z-C21.2, finding L12-1. check_overhangs called GetBodies2(swSolidBody, true), and IPartDoc~GetBodies2.html says of the second argument: «True gets only the visible bodies, false gets all of the bodies in the part». A body hidden to look inside the part dropped out of the analysis without anything saying so, and the answer was «it prints without supports» on a part that has a body that overhangs.
defect_caught: Two bodies: a straight block, which prints, and its copy tapered at 60 degrees as in `walls_at_sixty_degrees_do_not_print`, which overhangs on four sides. The copy is HIDDEN before the check («hide_first», with the body of its front face in front). On the old library the check looks only at the straight block and answers 0 overhanging faces; on the new one the four walls of the copy are there.
_and_what_if_the_hidden_body_does_not_te: The guide does not say whether GetTessTriangles answers on a hidden body (the mini-probe of the entry is still to be run). Here it does not matter: the four walls are PLANAR, and for a planar face the fallback on IFace2.Normal is exact. If they tessellate they are counted by triangles, if not by normal: 4 in both cases.
_where_the_faces_are: The block goes from x = -50 to 50, the copy (dx = 200) from 150 to 250. The faces are named by the point the state publishes, GetClosestPointOn(0,0,0): for the copy it falls at x = 150 (front, left, top, bottom) and at x = 250 (right); for the block at x = 0, -50 and 50.

expect.why: it narrows towards the bottom: it is the upside-down frustum, the shape that overhangs (see `walls_at_sixty_degrees_do_not_print`)
the four walls at 60 degrees of the HIDDEN copy. On the old library: 0

expect.tolerance_why: the angle is derived from the normals of the triangles, which are single-precision floating point

expect.why: the answer says that a hidden body was looked at
